(CNN) -- A one-of-a-kind bicycle belonging to U.S. cycling legend Lance Armstrong was stolen from a team truck in California, just hours after he rode it Saturday on the opening day of a nine-day race.

Armstrong, a cancer survivor and seven-time Tour de France champion, is competing in the Amgen Tour of California this week as he continues his latest comeback after retiring from the sport in 2005. His first comeback came in 1998, two years after he was diagnosed with advanced testicular cancer that had spread to his lungs and brain. Doctors had given him a less than 50 percent chance of survival.

Armstrong announced the theft Sunday morning on his Twitter account and posted a photograph of the bike.

“There is only one like it in the world therefore hard to pawn it off. Reward being offered,” the Texan wrote before going on to finish fifth in Sunday’s testing first stage, won by Spain’s Francisco Mancebo.

Swiss Olympic champion Fabian Cancellara, who began the day in the yellow jersey after winning Saturday’s time-trial prologue, withdrew midway through the stage after feeling unwell.

Armstrong moved up from 10th to fifth overall, one minute and five seconds behind the leader, while his Astana teammate Levi Leipheimer, the two-time defending champion, stood in second place behind Mancebo.

“Holy hell. That was terrible,” said Armstrong, who suffered a puncture. “Maybe one of the toughest days I’ve had on a bike, purely based on the conditions. I’m still freezing.”

The stolen bicycle is not the one Armstrong rides every day during the race. It is used only for time trials, events in which cyclists ride individually at staggered intervals over a set distance and compete for the fastest time.

The thieves took four bicycles from a truck that Armstrong’s Astana team had parked behind a hotel in Sacramento. The other three belonged to team members Janez Brajkovic, Steve Morabito and Yaroslav Popovych, Astana said.

Armstrong, 37, won the Tour de France, widely considered the world’s premier bicycle race, a record seven times from 1999 to 2005.

The 750-mile Amgen Tour of California ends Sunday. It is the second major race Armstrong has entered since announcing his comeback in September. Last month, he competed in the Tour Down Under in Australia, finishing 29th.

Armstrong has said he is aiming for another Tour de France victory this summer and was not expected to contend in the Australian race, which he used to assess his fitness after more than three years out of the saddle.
